message_source_quote: I built Raman et al.'s vector exactly (35 DM think/don't-think pairs, k=6, band 20–24) and it collapses pass@10 to 0 — as does *any* comparable band push, including random directions, and the one-sided scene contrast.
writeup_source_quote:
The slot term takes the stance-steering idea of Raman et al. 2026 (white-bear steering,
`papers/`) but uses a different stance — production readiness, not the holding stance — because
on this server their recipe (k = 6, band 20–24) and indeed any comparable band push, even random,
collapse pass@10 to ~0, as does the one-sided scene contrast.

differences.message_quote: Their 0.83 was measured at WSB's read cell (final prompt token); your server's read cell sits at the template tail / assistant prefill (calibrated: capture "last" ≠ "user", and frame correction only bites at "read").

rationale: Both documents credit Raman et al. 2026 (white-bear steering) as the basis for the method's slot term and both report that the authors' exact recipe collapses pass@10 to ~0 on this server, motivating the switch to a different ('production-readiness') stance. The message goes further than the write-up by diagnosing a likely cause for the non-reproduction (a read-cell position mismatch between WorkspaceBench and this server) and recommending it be noted in the source paper and checked with the server maintainer, details the write-up's terser 'Where it came from' section omits.
